::: {.callout-note title="Practice entry, written in hindsight" icon=false}
This entry was written in November 2026, after the outcome was known, to
practise the journal's method on a past market day. The prediction shows what
the mechanism would have implied that evening. It is not part of the scored
record.
:::

## Observation
<!-- REWRITE: why is it informative that two similar companies moved in opposite directions? -->

- MSFT +15.51%, its best day since 2008. META -7.95% on the same day.
- AMD +13.0%, SMH +6.9%, QQQ +3.30%.
- Healthcare -2.4% and defensives -1.6%. The 10-year yield rose slightly to 4.66%.

## Mechanism
<!-- REWRITE: what exactly did Microsoft show that Meta did not? -->

- Channel: cash flows.
- Microsoft beat expectations on cloud growth and did not raise its spending plans.
- Meta missed on earnings and raised its spending forecast, and its free cash flow fell sharply.
- The market rewarded AI spending that was already producing revenue.
- Yields did not fall, so this rally came from earnings, not from lower rates.

## Prediction
<!-- REWRITE: the two stocks ended close together. Was 60% too confident? -->

- 60% probability that MSFT outperforms META over the next five trading days (to August 6).
- Reasoning: after a large earnings surprise, prices often keep drifting in the same direction as analysts revise estimates.
- Wrong if META returns more than MSFT over that window.

## Scoring

- **Right, narrowly.** MSFT +10.8%, META +9.4%.
- The link held, but Meta rebounded almost as much once the whole market rallied.
- Lesson: a relative call (A beats B) removed the market direction from the bet, which is why it survived a strong week for everything.
